wizard.title: Set up your workspace
wizard.intro: Three short steps. Provider setup is optional until your first model use, you can skip anything and come back later, and no advanced configuration is forced.
wizard.resumeIntro: Welcome back. Re-running setup never resets your existing choices.
wizard.skipDone: Setup skipped. You can resume it any time from this page or from Settings, Connections.
wizard.preservationPolicy: Going back keeps what you entered in this session. Nothing you enter here is kept after you close the app, and your API key is never kept at all — not in browser storage, not in links, not in logs.

completion.help: Setup completion is recorded only after the Core confirms it. The Core connection contracts are not wired in this milestone, so completion cannot be recorded yet. Skipping keeps your choices and loses nothing.
completion.unavailableBody: The completion request was not submitted: the Core connection contracts are not wired in this milestone, so there is no Core to confirm completion. Nothing was sent, and no completion was recorded.
completion.unavailableNote: Your choices are kept. You can skip and return later.

leaveGuard.title: Leave with unsaved entries?
leaveGuard.body: This form has entries that are not saved. Nothing was sent to a Core. You can keep editing, discard the entries, or try to save them now.
leaveGuard.saveNote: Saving reports its real result: the Core provider contracts are not wired in this milestone, so a save attempt reports that it was not submitted.

step1.heading: Choose your connection
step1.help: This choice tells the app which Core you intend to work with. It never moves or copies Jobs or data between Cores.
step1.localHelp: Work with a Core running on this machine.
step1.remoteHelp: Work with a Core over the network. Establishing a Remote or Team connection needs the Core bootstrap and session contracts, which are not wired in this milestone — the connection itself is established when those contracts are wired.
step1.recorded: Your choice is kept on this device and can be changed later.

bootstrap.heading: Connect to your local Core (interim manual step)
bootstrap.help: When the Core's local transport is running, it can exchange a one-time bootstrap credential for a session. This panel is the interim manual path: you paste the credential the Core issued through its trusted-local channel. The full browser bootstrap flow (automatic launch and hand-off) is a separately tracked decision and is not built here.
bootstrap.credentialHelp: Paste the bootstrap- credential exactly as issued. It is a one-time secret: it stays in this page's memory only, is sent once to your local Core, and is never stored in the browser, in a link, or in a log.
bootstrap.successBody: The one-time credential was exchanged exactly once for a session. The session token is held in this page's memory only — never written to browser storage — and it expires at the Core-set time shown below.
bootstrap.sessionExpiredNote: The session this page held is no longer authorized by the Core. The token has been discarded from memory; you can connect again with a fresh one-time credential.
bootstrap.failureNote: Nothing was retried automatically. A new attempt is a new explicit action by you.
bootstrap.failureUnreachableBody: No Core transport answered at this app origin, so the Core received nothing to exchange. The Core's local transport is opt-in and disabled by default; verify the Core is running with its local transport enabled and that this page's origin is configured to reach it.
bootstrap.failureUnknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof of success or failure: a one-time credential may or may not have been consumed, and only the Core knows. If the Core shows no session, connect again with a fresh credential — never with the same one.
bootstrap.failureSessionInvalidBody: The Core refused the credential ({{code}}): it is unknown to this Core, already used, expired, or was issued for a different origin than this page. A credential can be exchanged exactly once, and a replayed credential also revokes the session it first minted.
bootstrap.failureBoundaryTitle: The Core's boundary refused the exchange
bootstrap.failureBoundaryBody: The Core's own boundary rules refused this request (reason: {{reason}}, code: {{code}}). Browser-originated requests are enforced by the Core; nothing was exchanged and nothing is worked around here.
bootstrap.failureValidationTitle: The exchange request was refused as invalid
bootstrap.failureValidationBody: The Core refused the exchange request as invalid ({{code}}{{field}}). Nothing was exchanged.
bootstrap.failureGenericBody: The Core refused the exchange (code: {{code}}). Nothing was exchanged. The code above is the Core's stable machine identifier.

step2.heading: Connect a provider (optional)
step2.help: You can skip this step until your first model use. A skipped provider always leaves a clear path back — from the next step, from the home page, or from Settings, Connections.

step3.heading: Choose your first action
step3.help: Pick what to do first. The flows below ship in later packages, so they are listed with their honest availability.
step3.chatNote: Not available yet: the chat surface ships in a later package.
step3.importNote: Not available yet: the import flow ships in a later package.
step3.templateWithheld: A sample workflow template would be listed here only if the Core actually ships one. None is offered in this milestone.
step3.safeActions: Safe actions available now: skip this setup and use the app. Settings is reachable from the navigation, and this setup can be resumed any time from the home page or from Settings, Connections.

provider.presetHelp: Choose a provider preset or Custom API. The preset list is fixed; Custom API lets you enter the endpoint details yourself.
provider.apiFormatUnavailable: API format options come from the Core's implemented, conformance-tested adapters. The provider contracts are not wired in this milestone, so the option list is unavailable.
provider.baseUrlHelp: The provider API endpoint. HTTPS is required for network endpoints; plain HTTP is allowed only for a local endpoint such as localhost.
provider.baseUrlInvalid: Enter a valid URL, for example https://api.example.com/v1
provider.baseUrlInvalidScheme: Only http and https URLs are accepted.
provider.baseUrlInsecure: Network endpoints must use HTTPS. Plain http is allowed only for a local endpoint such as localhost or 127.0.0.1.
provider.baseUrlEmbeddedCredentials: URLs with an embedded username or password are not accepted. Enter the endpoint without credentials.
provider.apiKeyRequired: Enter the API key or token for this connection.
provider.apiKeyHelp: Your key stays in memory only while this form is open. It is sent only when you run Test connection or Save securely, it is never stored in the browser, and it is never shown again after a successful save.
provider.modelIdRequired: Enter the model ID to verify.
provider.modelIdHelp: The model identifier to verify and use, exactly as the provider names it.
provider.headersHelp: One header per line, in the form Name: value. Header values stay in memory with the rest of this form and are never stored in the browser.
provider.headersInvalid: One or more lines do not match the Name: value form.
provider.billingLabel: Your API key / your provider billing
provider.billingNote: This connection uses your own API key, and usage is billed by your provider. It is separate from any product maintenance plan.
provider.dataHandlingBody: Your API key and entries stay in memory while this form is open and are never written to browser storage, links, logs, or telemetry. Verification and storage happen only through the Core's credential boundary, which is not wired in this milestone. Provider-specific data-handling details are supplied by the Core once it is connected.
provider.testHelp: Read-only: verifies the endpoint and model and reports confirmed capabilities. Nothing is stored.
provider.saveHelp: Stores the provider metadata and the key through the Core's credential boundary, then clears the key from this form.
provider.testUnavailableBody: The test was not submitted: the Core provider contracts are not wired in this milestone, so there is no Core to run the test against. Nothing was sent, and nothing was verified.
provider.testUnavailableNote: Your entries are preserved, including the key field. Nothing left this device.
provider.saveUnavailableBody: The save was not submitted: the Core provider contracts are not wired in this milestone, so nothing was stored. Your non-secret entries are preserved; the key field was cleared.
provider.saveUnavailableNote: You can enter the key again and retry — it is never restored from storage, because it is never stored.
provider.capabilityNote: Capabilities appear here only after a real verification through the Core. Until then they stay Not verified — nothing is inferred from the provider or model name.
provider.validationSummary: Some fields need attention before this connection can be tested or saved.
